measures:
HOW THE GATE MEASURES - build to these definitions exactly

  Every run is headless (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy, SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy) at seed 7 (and identically at one undisclosed seed), in a FRESH EMPTY working directory: the gate calls gilded.settings.settings_path() and gilded.save.quicksave_path() there and deletes both first, and it deletes a game-named file ONLY if that file's directory is the block's temp working directory (otherwise every line of the block FAILS with "... escapes the working directory: <path>"). A launch is pygame.display.quit() then gilded.ui.app.new_app_state(seed=7, start="game"); the gate then sets the player's stake through game.ambitions.set_ambition(house, F) (F = Dynasty at seed 7; the undisclosed seed picks another family) and calls gilded.agenda.ensure_agenda(game, h) for every rival. A draw is widgets.take_text_rows(), view.regions.clear(), view.draw(<the live display surface>); the drawn text is widgets._text_rows (blit_text records one row per call) - every fact's HOME below must be drawn through blit_text. The gate ALSO records every string any font's render() produces during a draw (it installs a recording pygame.font.Font and clears widgets._font_cache before its first draw): text rendered through any font - font.render + surface.blit outside blit_text included - counts when the gate looks for a SECOND home or a leak (C11.1b, C11.1c, C11.3b). A fact drawn outside blit_text cannot be the home, and it can still be the leak. A LINE is the text rows whose centre-y lie within 6 px of each other, joined left to right with spaces. A line BELONGS to the house whose name appears first in it (whole word). A press of End Turn is: draw, the drawn {"end_turn": True} region must be the top region at its centre, view.handle_click(centre), then gilded.ui.app._apply_action(state, that dict); game.turn must advance by one.

  INTEL STATES. The gate builds what a rival house R reads of the player from the sim's own sources and verifies each state with gilded.intel.report(game, R, player).tier (gilded/intel.py is not yours to change - every state below must stay reachable): it first strips R's sources on the player (game.houses[R].relations[player] = 0, no marriage tie tuple between them in game.marriages.marriages, no Secret on the player's ruler held by a member of R's dynasty, (R, player) not in game.informants) - at turn 1 that is tier 0 - then adds, in any combination: an informant ((R, player) into game.informants), diplomatic ties (game.houses[R].relations[player] = 5), a held secret (a gilded.society.characters.Secret on the player's ruler whose holders include R's ruler). Each source is one tier step (intel.py's own rule).

  THE CENSUS (C11.1b, C11.1c, C11.3b): every screen the play view can show - for each spine in gilded.ui.broadsheet.TABS, every page in view.house_pages (House) / view.powers_pages (Powers) - PLUS every page named by a drawn {"tab": T} or {"set_spine_page": P} region on any screen. A Powers page is drawn once with view._powers_selected = None ("Powers/<page>") and once with each rival selected ("Powers/<page>[<rival>]"); each of those is a screen of its own. The HUD strip and the bottom bar are part of every screen they are drawn on. Pickers stay closed.

  C11.1a.rival-reads-you: for two rivals R (the seed picks them), the gate walks R through nine intel states on the player, in this order: none (tier 0), informant (1), informant + ties (2), ties (1), ties + informant (2), ties + informant + secret (3), ties + secret (2), secret (1), none (0) - so adding and removing the informant flips the tier across 2 in both directions, an informant alone is tier 1, and tier 2 is also reached with no informant at all. In each state it draws Powers/Dossier with R selected (view.powers_page = "Dossier", view._powers_selected = R) and reads the LINES that belong to R. The reads-you line is a line belonging to R (e.g. "House R reads your ambition (their intel on you 2/3)") whose text is not the same in all nine states. In EVERY state at least one such line must be drawn, and it must state the sim's answer as read at draw time: when report(game, R, player).tier >= 2 (R sees the player's family) none of R's changing lines may carry a negation word; when the tier is 0 or 1 at least one of them must. The negation words, matched as whole words in any letter case: not, no, cannot, can't, cant, never, nothing, none, nor, without, unable, unaware, blind, unseen, unknown, hidden, hide, hides, dark, guess, guesses, guessing, and any word ending in n't (doesn't, isn't, ...). "fog" is NOT on the list: the campaign's own phrase "House R reads your ambition through the fog" is safe in the seeing form. So "House R cannot read your ambition" / "House R reads your ambition" works; a statement that follows the informant, the ties, the tier number or a value cached at first draw does not.

  C11.1b.reads-you-never-names: no reads-you line (any changing line of C11.1a, any state) may name the player's family in any spelling (the family word in any case, and its stems: conquest/conquer..., dominion..., buyout/buy-out..., dynast... (dynasty, dynastic), intrigu..., glory/glories/glorious..., consolidat...) or carry the stake's why text (game.ambitions.status(player)["why"]). Nor may it name the family in other words: the line is the same text whatever family the player holds - for each of the two rivals, at tier 0 (no sources) and at tier 2 (ties + informant), the gate draws Powers/Dossier with R selected, swaps the stake with game.ambitions.set_ambition(player, F2) for another family, draws again, then restores the stake; the screen's drawn text (LINES and rendered strings) must be identical across the swap. A paraphrase of the family ("your plan to wed the great houses") is a name. And with the first rival reading the player at tier 2 (ties + informant), a census of every screen must find the player's family word (whole word, any case, lines and rendered strings) on exactly ONE screen, a House one (the Court in Session, C10's home for it) - so the family may not appear beside the reads-you line in rendered ink either.

  C11.1c.reads-you-one-home: for each of the two rivals, the gate censuses every screen with R at ties only (tier 1) and again with ties + informant (tier 2). The screens whose drawn text (LINES and rendered strings, as a multiset) differ between the two must be exactly Powers/Dossier[R]: not Powers/Overview with R selected, not the HUD, not any other screen.

  THE COURTSHIP RUN (C11.2a, C11.2b, C11.2c, C11.3a, C11.3b): one launch per seed, the stake set as above, every rival's agenda ensured. If the player's house (or House T2 below) holds no adult that game.ambitions.wants(house) says opposes, the gate gives its first non-ruler adult (by id) a disposition of -60 x polarity on the family's own line (gilded.ambitions.FAMILY_DISPOSITION). The gate wraps gilded.ai.ai_turn (the chassis imports it from gilded.ai inside end_turn) and, before each AI house X's turn, sets X's intel: House A (the seed picks it) is given informant + ties on the player and every source it has on every OTHER house is stripped (A reads the player at tier 2 and nobody else); House A2 is given ties + a held secret on House T2 (tier 2, no informant) and every other source of A2's is stripped, the player included; House B holds an informant on the player and nothing else (tier 1); House C holds ties with the player and nothing else (tier 1); the other rival is left as the sim plays it. The tier an AI house HOLDS on a house is report(game, X, house).tier read as X's ai_turn begins - the courtship reads the intel the house holds as its turn opens (a marriage or an informant won during that turn counts from its next turn). The gate then presses End Turn 4 times. During each ai_turn(game, X) it compares, for every other house H, each living adult (age >= 16) of H before and after: a member is COURTED when, during X's ai_turn, either their stance in game.ambitions.wants(H) changed (they are still a living adult of H), or they left game.realms[H].characters and ARRIVED, alive, in the courting house's own game.realms[X].characters with no new marriage tuple in game.marriages.marriages naming them. A member struck from the realm with no destination is not courted, nor is a death, nor a wedding. A courtship is NAMED when a Beat appended to game.beats.log during that same ai_turn has the member's full name (character.name) in its text.

  C11.2a.ai-courts-the-player: within House A's first 3 AI turns, A courts a member of the player's house whom wants(player) said opposes as A's turn began, and the courtship is named. A beat without a stance change or a departure is not a courtship; a stance change or a departure without a beat naming the member does not count.

  C11.2b.ai-courts-a-rival-house: within House A2's first 3 AI turns, A2 courts a member of House T2 whom wants(T2) said opposes, and the courtship is named - the AI pulls the lever on any house it reads at tier >= 2, not only on the player, and tier 2 without an informant counts.

  C11.2c.courts-only-through-intel: over the whole run, at least one courtship happened, NO member of any house H was courted during the AI turn of a house X that held tier 0 or 1 on H as that turn began (Houses B and C, informant-only and ties-only, are tier 1 on the player), and no member was courted who did not oppose their own house's ambition as the turn began.

  C11.3a.rival-lever-on-court: right after the End Turn press during which House A first courted one of the player's opposers with a named beat, the gate draws House/Court (view.house_page = "Court"): a LINE must be drawn there that names the member (full name) and House A (whole word), that was not drawn on House/Court just before that press, and that names no other living adult of the player's house and no other rival house (one line per lever; a list of the whole court or of every rival is not the lever). Names are not unique (seed 7's court has three "Khufu Ashworth"): the gate matches the courted member's full name (character.name).

  C11.3b.rival-lever-one-home: in that same state, a census of every screen: no screen but House/Court may draw a line or a rendered string naming both that member and House A (not the HUD, not the bottom bar, not Powers/Dossier with A selected).

  C11.9: the C10 gate (and through it C1..C9) still passes, run in a fresh interpreter.

work.title: The AI courts a rival's opposing member as a lever when it reads that house at intel tier >= 2, and a beat names the member
work.text: gilded/ai.py, ai_turn(game, house): as the AI house's turn opens (before its docket and initiative), it looks over the other houses it reads at gilded.intel.report(game, house, target).tier >= 2 and courts ONE adult of such a house whom game.ambitions.wants(target) says opposes that house's ambition (not the ruler). The lever the committed suite accepts is the STANCE: the member's disposition on the target's family line (gilded.ambitions.FAMILY_DISPOSITION) moved into the wary band, so wants(target) stops saying opposes; they stay at their house. The other lever - the member leaves the target house for the courting house's court (out of game.realms[target].characters, into game.realms[house].characters, any court seat they held left vacant, no marriage tuple) - is the version that tipped test_c2_contract's grid and test_ai's attention pin; if you take it, the member must ARRIVE in your court (a member struck from the realm with no destination is not courted). Either way a gilded.beats.Beat appended through game.beats.append names them in its text (e.g. "House K courts <member> of House P"), with house = the target and a facet the court page can find (e.g. "rival_lever"). Nothing at tier 0 or 1 (an informant alone, or ties alone, is tier 1), nothing for members who do not oppose, at most one courtship per AI turn and at most one per house per 10 turns (a commit window - more drifts the 50-turn centuries test_endings_read_the_reign pins), one attention point per courtship, and keep the AI's other behaviour (attention, initiatives, matchmaking) as test_ai.py pins it. gilded/tests/test_c11_rivals.py asserts C11.2a-c as written in measures by wrapping gilded.ai.ai_turn.

rules: Clarity Law: state, in test_c11_rivals.py's module docstring and in the commit message, which spine/inner page owns each new piece of content - whether a rival reads your ambition: Powers/Dossier with that rival selected; a lever a rival pulled on your house: House/Court - and prove nothing else shows it with a test that draws EVERY reachable screen (every spine, every page, every page a drawn set_spine_page region names, every Powers page with each rival selected) and finds the fact on exactly one. The player's family word keeps its one home (House/Court, C10.1b).
Headless runs only: SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy and SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy before importing pygame.

Every drawn fact goes through blit_text (widgets._text_rows) - text rendered with font.render + blit is still on the screen and the gate counts it as a second home or a leak; tiers, stances and beats are read from the sim (gilded.intel.report, game.ambitions.wants, game.beats.log) at draw time, never cached or pasted.

The AI cheats at nothing: a courtship reads the intel the AI house holds as its turn opens (gilded.intel.report), changes the sim (a stance off opposes, or the member leaves the house and arrives, alive, in the courting house's court - a member struck from the realm with no destination is not courted, nor a death, nor a wedding) and leaves a Beat in game.beats.log naming the member; an AI house never writes informants, relations, marriages or secrets to raise its own tier for a courtship.

Keep the committed censuses and controls green: for GildedGame(seed=42) with no ambition, test_ui_broadsheet's EXPECTED_REGIONS House 32 / Powers 19 / Atlas 32 regions and the Governance picker-open census of 21 regions, test_c6c_layout's control groups, test_ui_hud_meters' hud_model keys, test_ui_actions_i4d2b1's 46 ACTIONS keys, test_c10_ambitions.py (the court cards, the levers, the ladder, the one home of the family word), test_ai.py's AI-turn pins (an AI turn that returns messages spent at least one attention point; initiatives; matchmaking), and test_c2_contract.py's grid (seed 7 Consolidation / 11 Glory / 13 Buyout: at least one stake fulfilled AND at least one falls short while a rival reads the player at tier 2 - a courtship that moves members out of the player's house can tip every stake to fulfilled; a stance change does not), and test_endings_read_the_reign.py's 50-turn verdict pair (a lever pulled by every house on every turn drifts the century enough to flip it; one lever per house per 10-turn commit window does not).
Do not special-case the disclosed seed; every line is repeated at an undisclosed seed.
Do not weaken, skip or mark any committed test.
